Q: geom_point with shape, fill and color A:

Now with scale_shape_manual as indicated by @erc, it worked:

plot3<-ggplot(example,aes(x=x_axis,y=mean , shape = cat.1)) +  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~time,dir = "h")+
  geom_jitter(aes(fill=cat.2), position = position_jitter(0), size=4, color="black")+
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())+
  geom_errorbar(aes(x_axis, ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd),
                position = position_jitter(0), width=0.1) +
  scale_shape_manual( values =c("x"=24,"y"=21))

Q: Adding a legend to ggplot2 facets with multiple lines? A:

This is how I've tweaked my code to get the multi-panel plots i wanted. Thanks to datanovia for the great reference materials! I've also included a legend. 

dahir %>% filter(is.na(Year) == FALSE) %>% 
ggplot(dahir, mapping = aes(x = Year, y = value)) + 
  geom_line(size = 1.2, aes(color = variable, linetype = variable)) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkred", "steelblue"))+
  labs(y="Index: 2012=100",
       title = "Decoupling by City")+
  facet_wrap (~City)

Decoupling in metropolitan cities

Q: Django Allauth email verification A:

Ensure you are using the latest version of `django-allauth`.

Also the docs say:

Setting `ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION` to "mandatory" requires "email*" to be listed in ACCOUNT_SIGNUP_FIELDS. You can have something like this in your settings:

ACCOUNT_SIGNUP_FIELDS = ['email*', 'password1*', 'password2*']

If error persists, please post your complete error log, allauth config in settings and your version of django-allauth.

Q: Is there a way to programmatically remove all blank pages from a PDF file? A:

An old question, but still, here is a new solution. pdftl can delete blank pages, like this:

pdftl in.pdf delete_blank output out.pdf

Disclaimer: I am the pdftl developer

Q: import "dotenv" could not be resolved A:

While working in a virtual environment, I tried several approaches, but nothing worked except this one:

# 1. Deactivate any existing venv
deactivate

# 2. Delete old venv (if corrupted)
rm -rf venv

# 3. Create new venv
python3 -m venv venv

# 4. Activate it
source venv/bin/activate

# 5. Upgrade pip inside venv
pip install --upgrade pip

# 6. Install packages
pip install python-dotenv

Q: VS Code main window is blank A:

Deleting the %appdata%\Code\User directory fixed the problem for me.

WARNING: This deletes your entire user preferences, and it's like doing a factory reset to VS Code. Ensure you have backed up your settings using Settings Sync, etc.
